'''Senta Amon Raizen''' (28 October 1924 – 23 December 2017) was an Austrian-born American scientist and educator.<ref>{{cite web |title=Senta Raizen Obituary - Falls Church, VA |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/en-ca/obituaries/falls-church-va/senta-raizen-7715809 |website=Dignity Memorial |access-date=26 February 2025 |language=en-ca}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Senta Raizen spent her childhood in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]] until the age of 13 when her parents sent her to study in the [[Netherlands]] and later at [[Sidcot School]] in [[England]] to escape the German occupation of Austria. She then transferred to [[George School]] in [[Pennsylvania]] when her parents immigrated to the [[United States]]. Raizen graduated [[Guilford College]] in 1944 and received a Master's degree from [[Bryn Mawr College]].<ref>{{cite web |title=I am a Supporter |url=https://peaceworks.afsc.org/senta-raizen/story/472 |website=Peace Works: Century of Action |access-date=26 February 2025 |language=en |date=19 December 2016}}</ref>

== Career ==
After college, Raizen worked as a chemist at [[Sunoco|Sun Oil Company]] and later as a science educator and Director at [[WestEd]].<ref>{{cite web |title=How to Support Beginning Teachers: Looking Beyond Our Borders |url=https://www2.wested.org/www-static/online_pubs/rd-02-02.pdf |publisher=WestEd |access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref> She founded the National Center for Improving Science Education and worked there until her retirement.<ref>{{cite web |title=SENTA RAIZEN Obituary (1924 - 2017) - Falls Church, VA - The Washington Post |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/washingtonpost/name/senta-raizen-obituary?id=6092859 |website=Legacy.com |access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref>

In 1991, Raizen spoke about improving the US school system at the National Education Goals Panel.<ref>{{cite web |title=National Education Goals Panel |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/public-affairs-event/national-education-goals-panel/15296 |publisher=National Cable Satellite Corporation |access-date=26 February 2025 |date=4 September 1991}}</ref>
{{Blockquote|text=It's all very well to test [learning] outcomes in terms of achievement. If we don't know what leads to those outcomes and how we need to change the [teaching] practices so we get better outcomes, then we can collect outcome information forever and we probably won't be improving very much.}}

The [[Virginia House of Delegates]] passed a resolution in 2018 celebrating Raizen's life and contributions.<ref>{{cite web |title=HOUSE JOINT RESOLUTION NO. 251: Celebrating the life of Senta Amon Raizen  |publisher=Virginia's Legislative Information System |url=https://legacylis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?181+ful+HJ251ER+pdf |access-date=26 February 2025 |date=22 February 2018}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Senta Raizen married Abraham Alfred "Al" Raizen and had three children, Helen, Michael, and Daniel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Abraham Alfred Raizen Collection |url=https://www.loc.gov/item/afc2001001.50122/ |website=Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. 20540 USA |access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref>
